correctness.rationale: The octahedron facet area is √3/2; its normal central section is the six vertices (e_i−e_j)/2, a regular hexagon of area 3√3/4 and self-area 3 (six unit-gauge sides divided by two). Eight facets in the recursive boundary integral give Ω3(O)=(8/3)(√3/2)(3/(3√3/4))=16/3. The product induction splits boundary of A×B into ∂A×B and A×∂B; the normal-section Euclidean volumes cancel, yielding Ω_{a+b}(A×B)=Ω_a(A)Ω_b(B). With Ω2(H)=3, Ω_{2k+1}(O×H^{k−1})=(16/9)3^k=(8/9)2·3^k. Independent rational check of facet/section area ratio and the product identity for k up to 34, not used as infinite proof.
